newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu says bombers got Palestinian go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says bombers got Palestinian go-ahead.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday the Palestinian Authority led by Yasser Arafat gave the green light for a suicide bombing in a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday.

"Every time there is an impasse or they have a grievance against us they send terrorists," Netanyahu said on ABC television's "This Week." "In this case they were sent a green light from the Palestinian Authority. On this we have absolute information."

Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority of violating its commitments to fight terrorism, annul the Palestinian charter calling for Israel's destruction, confiscate illegal weapons and desist from hostile propaganda.
Both Netanyahu and the U.S. State Department's Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross denied that Washington had urged the formation of a unity government in Israel.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, asked on the CBS programme "Face the Nation" if Arafat had given a "green light" for violence, said: "There is clearly perception of the green light but no concrete evidence."
Albright said Arafat had to do more to stop violence.

"There have been efforts on his part, 100 percent efforts, to stop the violence and the terrorism, but the result has not been 100 percent," she said. "He has condemned the violent acts, but there needs to be some improvement."
